quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: What should you do to stay in control of your motorcycle while turning?

options.text: Speed up before you enter the turn.
Look ahead through the turn to see what's coming.
Stop completely before you enter the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead through the turn to see what's coming.
questions.explanation: To stay in control during a turn, look ahead through the turn. Turn only your head to do this. Slow down before the turn and lean your motorcycle in the direction you are turning.

questions.question: When you carry a passenger, you should tell them to:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Get on the motorcycle after you start the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on the motorcycle after you start the engine.
questions.explanation: Give your passenger complete safety instructions before riding. Have them get on only after you start the engine. They should sit as close to you as possible without crowding you. They should hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt. They must keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: Drivers entering the highway from the right may not see your motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left side of your lane so they can share it if needed.
Change to another lane if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change to another lane if needed.
questions.explanation: Give plenty of space to vehicles entering the highway. Move to a lane farther from the entrance ramp if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to make room for them to enter safely.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When you change lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
Turn your head and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see if it is safe to change lanes.

questions.question: Bright-colored helmets:

options.text: Help other drivers see you better.
Don't help you be more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help other drivers see you better.
questions.explanation: A bright-colored helmet is a good choice. It protects your head if you crash, and the bright color helps other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Grip the handlebars tight and slowly release the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars tight and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—it will make things worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slowly release the throttle to slow down, and lean your weight forward and down. Pull over as soon as you safely can.

questions.question: To lean your motorcycle when turning, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip opposite to the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To turn, your motorcycle must lean. Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn to make the motorcycle lean.

questions.question: Before riding, check your tires for all of the following except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Flexibility.
questions.explanation: Before you ride, check your tire air pressure, tread, and signs of wear or damage.

questions.question: Approved helmets:

options.text: Can make it hard for you to see.
Let you see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
Don't need to be worn if you think your view is limited.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let you see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: Some people worry that helmets limit vision, but this is not true. An approved helmet allows you to see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: What is a major effect of drinking alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slower body functions.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down your body and mind.

questions.question: When you stop, how should you use the brakes?

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.
Use only one brake, front or rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop. Apply them at the same time.

questions.question: A helmet will NOT give the best protection if:

options.text: It is approved by the DOT.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has cracks.
questions.explanation: A good helmet must be approved by the DOT, fit snugly, and have no damage such as cracks, loose padding, or torn straps.

questions.question: Your body removes about one drink per hour. If someone drinks seven drinks in three hours, how many drinks are likely still in their system three hours later?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: To find how many drinks remain, subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Seven drinks minus six hours (three hours drinking plus three hours after) equals one drink removed per hour, leaving four drinks.

questions.question: What should you do to be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride very close to the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on.
questions.explanation: The most important thing you can do to help others see you is to keep your headlight on. Your headlight should be on whenever you ride.

questions.question: When riding past stopped or slow cars, you should:

options.text: Pull over and wait for traffic to move.
Ride on the shoulder to get through quickly.
Weave between cars to get through quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not weave between cars.
questions.explanation: Riding between parked or slow cars is dangerous. Car doors can open, or cars can pull out suddenly. You won't have room to escape. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers won't expect you there.

questions.question: Before riding, check everything except:

options.text: How much air is in your tires.
How much tread is on your tires.
The condition of your tire sidewalls.

questions.correctAnswerText: How reflective your tires are.
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire pressure, tread wear, and the condition of the sidewalls and tread.

questions.question: What is the main active ingredient in marijuana?
questions.correctAnswerText: THC
questions.explanation: The main active ingredient in marijuana is THC, short for tetrahydrocannabinol.

questions.question: When a vehicle passes you from behind, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
On the left side of the lane.
On the right side of the lane.
It doesn't matter where you are in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Staying too close to the passing vehicle increases your risk of a crash.

questions.question: If another vehicle is following you too closely, what should you do?

options.text: Let the other vehicle pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the other vehicle pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. If it is safe, change lanes and allow them to get ahead of you. Speeding up may make things more dangerous.
